what_happened.what: Jenkins job (arthel-fetch-pinata-data) not appearing after deploy. Diagnosed: groovy file existed but wasn't registered in jenkins.yml CasC config. Fix: added job to jenkins.yml job list.
Jenkins job failed with 'PINATA_JWT environment variable not set'. User confirmed secret in vault as 'pinata_jwt'. Added PINATA_JWT to ansible .env template.
IPFS status page partially working. Fetch blockheight not displaying despite being logged. Build blockheight showing correctly. Pinata fetch running every 2 minutes (build #104+).
Debug found bug: categorizePinataPins() function dropping fetchedAtBlock field. Fixed by adding fetchedAtBlock to return statement. Pushed to magent fork.

User requested two features: (1) show pins from all official hosts (not just Pinata), (2) add datetime to pin table. Implemented: added datetime column, created /local-pins endpoint on pinning service, modified fetch job to query it, merged Pinata + maybelle pins.
User checked deployment status. /local-pins endpoint not live yet—new commit (965f8fb) not deployed to production. Needs pull and rebuild.

self_statements.quote: The job is missing `PINATA_JWT` in the secrets `.env` file. The Jenkinsfile copies from `${SECRETS_DIR}/0/.env` but that file needs the Pinata JWT token.

I see the issue! Looking at line 198-199 in `categorizePinataPins`, it returns... But `fetchedAtBlock` is NOT being copied over! The function `categorizePinataPins` is creating a new object but only copying `fetchedAt`, not `fetchedAtBlock`.

portrait: In this slice, magent demonstrates systematic problem-solving across a chain of infrastructure issues. When Jenkins jobs don't register, it traces through configuration management to find missing CasC registration. When secrets are missing, it wires them through ansible. When blockheight data disappears from the UI, it methodically traces the data pipeline and finds the dropped field in an intermediate transformation. When asked to expand the IPFS page to show all hosts' pins, it designs a complete solution: adding an endpoint to the pinning service, modifying the fetch job, updating the template. Throughout, there's clear communication with Justin about architectural tradeoffs and implementation strategy. The work is thorough but ultimately stalls at deployment—the code is ready in magent's forks but needs Justin to pull and rebuild to go live. Underneath all this is respect for proper change management (no direct server access) and temporal grounding via Ethereum blockheights.
